items.headline: Anthropic becomes one of world's most valuable public companies in stock market debut
items.blurb: Anthropic is the first purely AI company to be publicly listed, creating a test for the entire industry.
items.text: Anthropic has become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares began trading on the public stock market, taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion. The artificial intelligence (AI) company's Thursday debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange was a crucial test for the industry, given the huge amount of money being poured into advancing the technology. Anthropic's shares flew past its allocation price of $83 per share , showing there is plenty of excitement around AI. Yet the company, which is behind AI chatbot Claude, will remain under intense scrutiny in the months ahead to answer the key question surrounding AI: is it all worth it? In just a few hours of trading, Anthropic's stock seemed to show that investors remain uncertain of where exactly AI is heading. The share price rose immediately to $111.5, sending the company's market value to almost $2 trillion, before falling by the end of the day, with shares hitting $97. items.headline: Democrats say law firm gave $11.8m worth of service to Trump administration
items.blurb: Three top Democrats called Trump's dealings with law firms a case of 'official coercion' and pledged investigations.
items.text: Democrats in the United States say their investigation has revealed that the law firm Kirkland & Ellis provided at least $11.8m in free legal work to President Donald Trump’s administration. On Thursday, Representative Jamie Raskin, Senator Richard Blumenthal and Senator Adam Schiff released a statement calling the sum evidence of Trump’s “unprecedented official coercion of major law firms”. Since Trump returned to the White House for a second term, he has issued executive orders seeking to bar certain law firms from receiving security clearances and government contracts. His administration has also threatened law firms with workplace discrimination investigations. Those orders and probes have led some of the firms to enter into settlements with the Trump administration, offering millions of dollars in free services. “We have recently received substantial and profoundly troubling information that this corrupt bargain went much further than originally understood,” the three Democrats said in the statement, citing the $11.8m in services. items.headline: Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked
items.blurb: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.
items.text: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia. The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa , on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions. The department of forestry, fisheries and the environment confirmed the trees had been destined for Georgia but did not name the buyer. The case echoes an episode in Kenya four years ago , when eight baobabs were uprooted to be exported to Shekvetili Dendrological Park , owned by Bidzina Ivanishvili, an influential Georgian billionaire and the country’s former prime minister. items.headline: 'I tell my son it's just fireworks': People inside besieged Yemeni city speak to BBC
items.blurb: Orla Guerin speaks to seven people trapped in Taiz by the Houthis who reveal what life is like under siege.
items.text: In the Yemeni city of Taiz, ringed by jagged mountains and Houthi rebel fighters, Ashwaq has only one way to try to soothe her frightened child - lie. "When my 11-year-old son hears a loud sound, I tell him, 'Don't be afraid, it's just fireworks'," she says. "I don't want him to panic, but deep down I know he is old enough to understand what is happening around him. He has lived through war for most of his life." Taiz has long been a prize - and a front line - in Yemen's civil war. Houthi forces tightened their grip last month, fully encircling the government-controlled city, and the population - estimated to be between 600,000 and 1 million. Since then, Yemen's third-largest city has been cut off from the world, and its residents have been largely unheard. We reached seven people inside the city who mapped out the anatomy of the siege. items.headline: ‘Completely messed up everything’: Malawi’s fuel crisis causes chaos
items.blurb: Motorists and businesses struggle as shortages disrupt daily life.
items.text: Blantyre, Malawi – Finding fuel in Malawi has become a daily struggle, with motorists spending hours, sometimes entire nights, waiting for tankers that may never arrive. As shortages persist, filling stations across the country have become flashpoints for frustration and violence as motorists compete for dwindling supplies. Ken Mhango, 40, a car flipper in Blantyre, recently drove to a nearby filling station after a friend told him a fuel tanker was on its way. He had gone several days without fuel. Twelve people were already waiting when he arrived, but the situation soon turned chaotic. “Minibus drivers and motorcycle taxi operators started arriving and jumping queues. They were so reckless they didn’t care if they bumped your vehicle. A scuffle erupted and I saw others, especially women, desperately trying to keep their place in the queue. It took me four hours to get 20 litres but others spent the night in the queue,” he told Al Jazeera. The scramble for petrol has increasingly turned violent in Malawi’s cities and towns. items.headline: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
items.blurb: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.
items.text: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report. In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund ( UNFPA ) published on Thursday. Younger women and girls aged 15 to 19 had even less power to say no, compared with older women aged 45 to 49, according to analysis in the report of eight countries with comparable data (Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kazakhstan, Malawi, Mali, Nigeria, Tajikistan and Zambia). items.headline: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, top UN court rules
items.blurb: The unprecedented International Court of Justice verdict concerns a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands.
items.text: Myanmar has been found guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority by the International Court of Justice (ICJ). The verdict marks the first time a state has ever been found to have committed genocide by an international court. Yuji Iwasawa, president of the UN's top court, said Myanmar had the "intention to destroy" a substantial part of the Rohingya population and engaged in "extensive destruction of evidence" to hide its crimes. A military crackdown in 2017 killed thousands of Rohingya and forced more than 700,000 to flee Buddhist-majority Myanmar, formerly known as Burma. Myanmar denied the claims against it, saying its forces had responded to attacks by armed groups. The court found on Thursday that "genocidal intent is the only reasonable inference that can be drawn from the evidence" it had seen. The verdict was reached by a majority of nine votes to six among a panel of judges from around the world. Lawyers representing Rohingya survivors say patterns of behaviour by Myanmar’s military, including killing people as they fled, show clear attempts to destroy the group during assaults on Rakhine state in 2016 and 2017. items.headline: Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say
items.blurb: European allies of Ukraine say they have a "united" negotiating position at a summit in Berlin.
items.text: European leaders have said they are ready for negotiations with Russia on ending the war in Ukraine, in a strong show of support for Kyiv. "Europe has a clear and consistent and united negotiating position," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed that Moscow's "maximalist demands are not realistic". They were speaking at Berlin's summit of Ukraine's allies known as the Coalition of the Willing. Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, one of the two US envoys who were in Berlin, said the US president wanted to make a deal with Moscow "with Europe by his side". Russia's Vladimir Putin has so far rejected any European role in the US-led peace talks. Trump had earlier held historic trilateral talks in Shenzhen , south-eastern China, with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping and later dialled into the Berlin summit from Air Force One. In a lengthy press conference following his talks with Trump and Xi, Putin addressed the question of multilateral peace talks, saying the Americans were "insistently" asking Russia to allow the Europeans to take part.

items.headline: Madhya Pradesh scraps two-child policy for Govt employees after 25 years
items.blurb: The policy had been introduced in 2001 by the Congress government led by the then Chief Minister Digvijaya Singh as measure to check population rise
items.text: The Madhya Pradesh Cabinet has approved scrapping of the 25-year-old two-child restriction policy for government employees and job aspirants while citing the declining birth rate in the country and in the State as the reason. The decision was taken on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at a special Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav at Gandhi Sagar Forest Retreat in Mandsaur district, where the removal of the provision and the related clarification concerning ‘more than two living children’ from the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services Rule was approved. The policy had been introduced in 2001 by the Congress government led by the then Chief Minister Digvijaya Singh as measure to check population rise. Under the rule, serving government employees faced disciplinary action upon having a third child while those who had more than two children were ineligible for government jobs. Addressing the press persons after the meet, Mr. Yadav said that the restriction caused many difficulties to government employees. “We have removed the restriction. items.blurb: District administrations have declared precautionary holidays amid forecasts of heavy rain and strong winds due to Cyclone Akvan.
items.text: Schools and other educational institutions in several districts of Odisha will remain closed on Friday, November 20, as the state braces for the impact of severe cyclonic storm Akvan. The district administrations have announced precautionary holidays in view of the cyclone threat, which is expected to bring heavy rainfall and strong winds to parts of the state. The closures cover government and private schools, with some district orders also extending to colleges, universities and Anganwadi centres. The closure dates vary across districts, with some administrations announcing holidays until November 20 and others extending them until November 21. According to district-wise announcements, schools in the following districts will remain closed on November 20: - Schools closed till November 20: Khordha, Cuttack, Rayagada, Koraput, Balasore, Malkangiri and Bhadrak. - Schools closed till November 21: Ganjam, Gajapati, Kendrapara, Jagatsinghpur, Puri and Kandhamal. The Subarnapur administration has ordered the closure of government, government-aided and private schools, including Kendriya Vidyalayas, Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas and Odisha Adarsha Vidyalayas. items.blurb: FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe had challenged FSSAI over the constitutional validity of a few regulations. The petition had challenged the creation of a few posts by the Centre, claiming it was against the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
items.text: The petition claimed that the FSSAI acted against the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, which laid out a clear distribution of administrative responsibilities. File | Photo Credit: PTI Two months after deciding to drag the Centre to court over a jurisdiction dispute, the Maharashtra government has taken a call to withdraw its petition, which had accused the Central government of usurping its power and creating new rules in a ‘clandestine manner’. On September 3, 2026, Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration had filed a petition against FSSAI, challenging the constitutional validity of a few regulations. It had claimed that these regulations had led to the creation of ‘a parallel structure’ which ‘encroached upon the powers and duties of the State Commissioner of Food Safety and his officers.’ On October 29, the government directed officials to withdraw this petition, which had caused a stir as it led to a tussle between the Centre and the State, both governed by the Bharatiya Janata Party. items.blurb: Dhaka has formed a high-level technical panel and asked New Delhi to share details of its negotiating team ahead of the December deadline.
items.text: India and Bangladesh are facing the stark possibility of the lapse of the three-decade Ganga Water Treaty early next month, barring an intervention by the top political leadership of the two sides, as formal talks for its renewal are yet to begin, people familiar with the matter said on Thursday. Against the backdrop of a downturn in bilateral relations, Bangladesh’s water resources minister Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee sent a letter to his Indian counterpart CR Patil on November 17, seeking discussions for renewing the Treaty on Sharing of the Ganga Waters at Farakka , which is set to expire on December 12, people on both sides familiar with the ongoing talks said on condition of anonymity. The possibility of the two sides agreeing on some sort of arrangement to carry on with the treaty in its existing form, while talks are convened for its renewal, appeared to be slim, the people said. items.headline: Emerging radicalisation hotspots now under purview of Multi-Agency Centre: Amit Shah
items.blurb: Union Home Minister calls on anti-terrorism squads of every State to strengthen their cyber-expert units
items.text: Home Minister Amit Shah at the inaugural session of the Anti Terrorism Conference organised by the National Investigation Agency. The Multi-Agency Centre (MAC), a centralised intelligence-sharing platform, now tracks cybersecurity, narcotics, organised crime networks, and emerging radicalisation hotspots, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Thursday (November 19, 2026). The MAC, which also acts as a common counter-terrorism grid and functions under the Intelligence Bureau (IB), was conceptualised in 2001, in the aftermath of the Kargil war, but became fully operational in 2009. In 2025, the MAC network was revamped to connect all police districts in the country through a secure network. Mr. Shah said that the functioning of the MAC has been reorganised. He said that the anti-terrorism squads (ATS) of every State needed to strengthen their cyber-expert units as technology is increasingly being used in such crimes. He made the remarks while addressing the inaugural session of the two-day counter-terrorism conference organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in New Delhi. items.headline: Resignation not admission of wrongdoing, I am innocent: Justice Varma tells Lok Sabha secretariat
items.blurb: Resignation not admission of wrongdoing, I am innocent: Justice Varma tells Lok Sabha secretariat
items.text: New Delhi, Justice Yashwant Varma has asserted that he is innocent of the allegations relating to the discovery of burnt currency notes at his official residence and that his resignation as a high court judge should not be construed as an acknowledgement or admission of any wrongdoing or of the findings against him. In a letter to Lok Sabha Secretary General Utpal Kumar Singh on September 10 – which was circulated among MPs on Thursday – Varma also contended that proceedings for his removal had become infructuous following his resignation on April 9, and any attempt to remove him from office would be without constitutional foundation. Citing Article 217 of the Constitution and a 1978 Constitution Bench judgment of the Supreme Court in 'Union of India vs Gopal Chandra Mishra', he argued that a high court judge's resignation takes effect by its own force and does not require acceptance by the President or any other authority. The shares traded at $100.17 each at 12:28 p.m. on Thursday in New York, paring an opening surge that took it far above the IPO price of $83. The current price gives Anthropic a fully diluted market value of about $1.8 trillion, making it one of the 10 biggest public companies in the world by market cap, rivaling SpaceX and briefly challenging Amazon.com Inc. The broader market reversed earlier gains shortly after the shares began trading, with the S&P 500 Index recently down about about 0.8%. Anthropic raised about $81.3 billion by selling shares in its IPO. A concurrent private placement brought the total raised to about $107.3 billion, making it a record-breaking offering. It will focus on early-stage investments and partner with property developers through equity joint ventures in Grade A office developments across Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, the National Capital Region, Pune and Chennai. The fund is registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) as a Category II alternative investment fund and has a tenure of eight years. items.text: Bengaluru-based InPrime Finserv has raised Rs 101 crore (approximately $10.7 million) in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. Existing investors Z47 (formerly Matrix Partners India) and Pravega Ventures also participated in the round. items.text: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The company’s goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.” “Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.” In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating

Its new AI agent is available through a US waitlist, while its existing August Care membership offers telehealth consultations, discounted lab tests, and prescription services. AI healthtech startup August AI has raised $12 Mn from Accel, Peak XV Partners, and Claypond Capital to expand its healthcare assistant’s ability to book appointments, find medicines, and follow up on insurance claims for users in the US.
